text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Metro voters reject amalgamation: Harris told to leave Toronto alone amid signs opponents to Conservative plan smell blood.
- Tories' reaction likely to be more flexibility.
- Ottawa forcing tobacco bill vote: Critics take protest to Montreal streets.
- Albania virtually shut down: Curfews, roadblocks appear under state of emergency.
- Serb mercenaries poised to fight for Zaire: Evidence surfaces of military contract between Milosevic and Mobutu to spirit fighters into Africa.
- Desjardins to slash 5,000 jobs: Financial co-ops will also sink C$550-million into technology and training to boost profit.
- Avenor cuts Repap offer to C$2.75-billion: New terms exclude B.C. unit seeking creditor protection.
- Successor named at Thomson: Head of newspaper unit to take over as CEO next January.
- Auto parts makers' business threatened by steel shortage: Duties make U.S. supply too costly.
- U.S. vultures looking for perch at Eaton's.
- Avenor cuts Repap offer: Forestry giant succombs to investor pressure and hammers out new deal that lops C$655 million form acquisition price.
